headword: {生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}

definitions.gloss: lifestyle habits; daily habits; way of living
definitions.explanation: The regular patterns and behaviors that make up one's daily life, including eating, sleeping, exercise, and other routines. Frequently used in health and medical contexts.

examples.japanese: {生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}を{見直|みなお}す。
{不規則|ふきそく}な{生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}が{健康|けんこう}に{悪影響|あくえいきょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: Irregular lifestyle habits have a negative effect on health.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}から{生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}を{改善|かいぜん}するように{言|い}われたので、{毎朝|まいあさ}ジョギングを{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: The doctor told me to improve my lifestyle habits, so I started jogging every morning.

notes:
Composed of {生活|せいかつ} (life, living) + {習慣|しゅうかん} (habit, custom). This compound is extremely common in health-related contexts, particularly when discussing prevention of diseases linked to diet, exercise, and sleep patterns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}を{改善|かいぜん}する — to improve lifestyle habits
- {生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん}を{見直|みなお}す — to review one's lifestyle habits
- {生活習慣病|せいかつしゅうかんびょう} — lifestyle-related disease (diabetes, hypertension, etc.)
- {規則正|きそくただ}しい{生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん} — regular lifestyle habits
- {不規則|ふきそく}な{生活習慣|せいかつしゅうかん} — irregular lifestyle habits

CULTURAL NOTE:
The term {生活習慣病|せいかつしゅうかんびょう} replaced the older term {成人病|せいじんびょう} (adult disease) in 1996 to emphasize that these conditions are linked to habits rather than age. This shift reflects Japan's strong public health emphasis on prevention.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {生活|せいかつ}リズム — life rhythm; focuses on the timing and regularity of daily activities
- {食生活|しょくせいかつ} — eating habits, dietary life; specifically about food
